sections.theory:
Central (federal) and provincial joint institutions

To carry out certain matters between the federal and provincial governments, such institutions have been established as relate equally to both the federal and the provincial governments, for example:

1. Planning Commission

2. Council of Common Interests

3. National Economic Council

4. National Finance Commission

5. Council of Islamic Ideology

The provincial governments

According to the 1973 constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan a parliamentary system has been introduced within the provinces. The executive head of each province is the Governor. The Chief Minister is the head of the provincial government, who runs the administration of the province with the help of provincial ministers and the Civil Secretariat. Each provincial minister has one or more departments, for whose performance he is responsible. At the provincial level there is an elected provincial assembly for legislation.

The provincial Governor

The importance that the President has as head in the country falls to the share of the Governor in the province. The duties and powers of the Governor are mentioned below.

Executive affairs

All provincial orders are issued in the name of the Governor. In most matters the Governor is bound by the advice of the Chief Minister and the provincial cabinet. It is the duty of the Chief Minister to keep the Governor informed of his performance. The Governor will also fulfil all those responsibilities that are laid on him from time to time by the President.

Judicial powers

When appointing the judges of the High Court, the President of the state also consults the Governor of the concerned province.

Duties during emergency

When an emergency is imposed in the whole country or any part of the country, then after the declaration of emergency, at the behest of the federal government the Governor can himself exercise all those powers which any provincial institution other than the provincial assembly had. Thus all executive powers pass to the Governor.

The provincial cabinet

Because the parliamentary principle prevails in the provincial government, the real executive powers belong to the provincial Chief Minister and his cabinet. According to Article 129 of the constitution, “the provincial government will exercise its powers regarding provincial administration in the name of the Governor.” In the provincial government the Chief Minister and the ministers will perform their duties under the supervision of the Governor, who will have the status of head. According to the constitution the Governor will appoint as Chief Minister that person who has the support of the majority of members in the concerned provincial assembly.

The provincial assembly

According to the constitution the provincial assembly consists of only one house. The number of seats in the provincial assemblies is as follows.

مرکزی (وفاقی) اور صوبائی مشترکہ ادارے

وفاقی اور صوبائی حکومتوں کے درمیان بعض امور کو سرانجام دینے کے لیے ایسے ادارے قائم ہیں جن کا تعلق وفاقی اور صوبائی حکومت دونوں سے یکساں ہوتا ہے۔ مثلاً

1۔ منصوبہ بندی کمیشن

2۔ مشترکہ مفادات کی کونسل

3۔ قومی اقتصادی کونسل

4۔ قومی مالیاتی کمیشن

5۔ اسلامی نظریاتی کونسل

صوبائی حکومتیں (The Provincial Governments)

اسلامی جمہوریہ پاکستان کے 1973ء کے آئین کے مطابق صوبوں کے اندر پارلیمانی نظام رائج کیا گیا ہے۔ ہر صوبے کا انتظامی سربراہ گورنر ہوتا ہے۔ وزیرِ اعلیٰ صوبائی حکومت کا سربراہ ہوتا ہے وہ صوبے کا انتظام صوبائی وزراء اور سول سیکرٹریٹ کی مدد سے چلاتا ہے۔ ہر صوبائی وزیر کے ذمے ایک یا ایک سے زیادہ محکمے ہوتے ہیں جن کی کارکردگی کا وہ ذمہ دار ہوتا ہے۔ صوبائی سطح پر قانون سازی کے لیے منتخب صوبائی اسمبلی ہوتی ہے۔

صوبائی گورنر

جو اہمیت ملک میں سربراہ کی حیثیت سے صدر کو حاصل ہوتی ہے وہی اہمیت صوبے میں گورنر کے حصے میں آتی ہے۔ ذیل میں گورنر کے فرائض و اختیارات کا ذکر کیا گیا ہے۔

انتظامی امور

تمام صوبائی احکامات گورنر کے نام پر کیے جاتے ہیں۔ بیشتر امور میں گورنر، وزیرِ اعلیٰ اور صوبائی کابینہ کے مشورہ کا پابند ہے۔ وزیرِ اعلیٰ کا فرض ہے کہ گورنر کو اپنی کارکردگی سے باخبر رکھے۔ گورنر ان تمام ذمہ داریوں کو بھی پورا کرے گا جو اس پر وقتاً فوقتاً صدر کی جانب سے عائد کی جائیں گی۔

صوبائی اسمبلی

آئین کے مطابق صوبائی اسمبلی صرف ایک ہی ایوان پر مشتمل ہوتی ہے۔ صوبائی اسمبلی میں نشستوں کی تعداد یوں ہے۔

Central (federal) and provincial joint institutions

To carry out certain matters between the federal and provincial governments, such institutions have been established as relate equally to both the federal and the provincial governments, for example:

1. Planning Commission

2. Council of Common Interests

3. National Economic Council

4. National Finance Commission

5. Council of Islamic Ideology

The provincial governments

According to the 1973 constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan a parliamentary system has been introduced within the provinces. The executive head of each province is the Governor. The Chief Minister is the head of the provincial government, who runs the administration of the province with the help of provincial ministers and the Civil Secretariat. Each provincial minister has one or more departments, for whose performance he is responsible. At the provincial level there is an elected provincial assembly for legislation.

The provincial Governor

The importance that the President has as head in the country falls to the share of the Governor in the province. The duties and powers of the Governor are mentioned below.

Executive affairs

All provincial orders are issued in the name of the Governor. In most matters the Governor is bound by the advice of the Chief Minister and the provincial cabinet. It is the duty of the Chief Minister to keep the Governor informed of his performance. The Governor will also fulfil all those responsibilities that are laid on him from time to time by the President.

Judicial powers

When appointing the judges of the High Court, the President of the state also consults the Governor of the concerned province.

Duties during emergency

When an emergency is imposed in the whole country or any part of the country, then after the declaration of emergency, at the behest of the federal government the Governor can himself exercise all those powers which any provincial institution other than the provincial assembly had. Thus all executive powers pass to the Governor.

The provincial cabinet

Because the parliamentary principle prevails in the provincial government, the real executive powers belong to the provincial Chief Minister and his cabinet. According to Article 129 of the constitution, “the provincial government will exercise its powers regarding provincial administration in the name of the Governor.” In the provincial government the Chief Minister and the ministers will perform their duties under the supervision of the Governor, who will have the status of head. According to the constitution the Governor will appoint as Chief Minister that person who has the support of the majority of members in the concerned provincial assembly.

The provincial assembly

According to the constitution the provincial assembly consists of only one house. The number of seats in the provincial assemblies is as follows.
